title: DreamerV3: Mastering Domains through World Models
hook: Instead of learning only from real experience, DreamerV3 builds a world model and practices inside its own imagination — one fixed config, 150+ tasks.
key_points: A general reinforcement-learning algorithm that learns a world model and improves from imagined rollouts.
With a single fixed configuration, outperforms specialized methods across 150+ diverse tasks.
Uses robustness techniques for stable learning across very different domains.
First method to collect diamonds in Minecraft from scratch — no human data or curricula.
content_html: Danijar Hafner, Jurgis Pasukonis, Jimmy Ba, and Timothy Lillicrap present DreamerV3, a general reinforcement-learning algorithm that learns a world model and then improves its behavior from "imagined" rollouts inside that model. With a single fixed configuration — no per-task tuning — it outperforms specialized methods across more than 150 diverse tasks.
extra_html:
How it works

DreamerV3 learns a model of how its environment responds to actions. Once it has that internal model, it can generate imagined rollouts and improve its policy from them, rather than relying solely on costly real-world trials. To make one configuration work across wildly different domains, the authors layer in robustness techniques that keep learning stable whether the task is a control problem or an open-ended game.

Why it matters

A single fixed setup clearing 150+ tasks is a strong signal of generality — most RL methods need careful per-task tuning. The headline demonstration is Minecraft: DreamerV3 is the first method to collect diamonds entirely from scratch, with no human data and no hand-built curriculum. Learning to plan inside a world model points toward agents that can practice efficiently before acting in the real world.
